items.title: Neverness to Everness Hosts Offline Event 'NTE PC Cafe Vacation' Starting August 21
items.summary: © Perfect WorldNeverness to Everness, a supernatural urban open-world RPG developed by Perfect World's Hotta Studio, is hosting its summer offline event 'Neverness to Everness PC C...
items.content:
Neverness to Everness, a supernatural urban open-world RPG developed by Perfect World's Hotta Studio, is hosting its summer offline event 'Neverness to Everness PC Cafe Vacation' from August 21 to 25.

The event is being held at GGX in Seoul and the T1 Base Camp Hongdae branch. Reserved seats operated under an advance booking system at T1 Base Camp sold out completely in less than 24 hours after opening. T1 Base Camp is an offline venue previously visited by esports players such as Faker and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang.

At the venue, visitors can play the game in a dedicated Neverness to Everness PC zone at no additional charge. Special menus and perks capturing the characters and summer atmosphere are provided on-site, alongside sales of event-exclusive merchandise and gift giveaways based on purchase amounts. A dedicated four-cut photo frame featuring characters and themes is also available.

At GGX, a stamp rally as well as cosplay and stage events featuring popular Espers such as Shinku, Lacrimosa, Nisha, and Zanhong will be held. A voice actor talk show, game creator showdowns, and a live drawing show are also scheduled to take place on-site.

Having introduced new content including the new character Zanhong, summer swimsuit costumes, and Volleyball Star through its Version 1.3 update, Neverness to Everness plans to expand player touchpoints through this offline event. Detailed information can be found on the official website, Lounge, YouTube, and X.

Image credit: Hotta Studio Guide by Callum Williams Guides Writer Updated on Aug. 19, 2026, 9:30 a.m. Follow Neverness to Everness Last updated : 19th August 2026 - Checked for new NTE codes. The latest anime gacha game on the block, Neverness to Everness (better known as NTE ) is, ostensibly, an open-world action RPG. Pretty part and parcel for these types of free-to-play games, I assumed, until I realised it was a full-on smorgasbord of open world mechanics. It's got a GTA-like wanted system, intricate combo-based combat, street racing, Yakuza-like mini-games, and a supernatural main story that has you challenging all manner of spooky monsters.

In short, it's serving pretty much every open-world staple on a kawaii-coded platter, and to get the most out of all of them, you'll want to make sure you're stocked up on resources. After all, if you're gonna cause havoc on the streets, you probably want a character that can stand up to the ire of the long arm of the law. One way to bag more of these resources is by using NTE's lineup of free codes to stash loot, like Beetle Coins, Annulith, and Fons. Luckily, we've compiled every active NTE code below, so you can start bankrolling your way through Hethereau with some fresh goodies.

Hello! Callum here. If you're wondering where you can go to hunt for more codes, well, I have two suggestions. Number one, bookmark this page! I'm always on the hunt for new codes, and if I spot any for NTE, I'll be throwing them in the list above as soon as possible. Pop in regularly and you'll always be up to date!

My second suggestion is to go ahead and follow the official NTE Discord server . When you're all signed up, you'll find a channel called " gift-code ". If you head over there, you'll find codes as they drop.

items.title: Neverness to Everness players find AI watermark left on Version 1.3 in-game artwork
items.summary: Chinese players found an unexpectedly familiar logo hiding in one of Version 1.3's assets.
items.content:
All News An AI logo was found in one of NTE's assets (image: Hotta Studios).

{" "} Neverness to Everness players find AI watermark left on Version 1.3 in-game artwork .iframe-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .img-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .a-img-media {aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} Chinese players found an unexpectedly familiar logo hiding in one of Version 1.3's assets. Neverness to Everness is facing another round of criticism over its use of generative AI after Chinese players spotted a Doubao watermark left on an in-game image. The artwork, which depicts a seahorse, appeared in Version 1.3 of the supernatural open-world RPG following its release in China on 12 August. Screenshots quickly began circulating among Chinese players before making their way to Reddit and X , with one detail making the source of the image particularly hard to miss: a visible watermark for ByteDance's AI assistant Doubao.

Doubao (豆包) is a generative AI assistant developed by TikTok parent company ByteDance, with tools covering text, image, and video generation, among other functions. Images and videos generated through its free tier carry a visible watermark.

Platforms : PC, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, iOS, Android, and Mac

Bilibili creator Wuxiang Xiaoyugan (五香小鱼干) was among the Chinese players who checked the image themselves, uploading a video showing the seahorse artwork in-game on 17 August. In the video, Wuxiang Xiaoyugan says they initially saw the image shared in a group chat and thought it looked AI-generated. They then logged into NTE to check and found the same asset, complete with the Doubao watermark.

A separate Bilibili discussion captured some of the Chinese player reactions, with screenshots of the comments later shared on X.

User Daidai Damowang (带带大魔王) confirmed they had checked the asset themselves: “I just logged in and checked, and it's real.”

Once that was settled, the comments quickly turned to what else Doubao might have been used for behind the scenes. Xuanyuan Xiaopangzhi (轩辕小胖纸) joked that “the code was probably written directly by Doubao,” while Heiyu Yemao (黑羽夜猫) imagined the request behind the seahorse itself: “Doubao, Doubao, help me generate a game asset image of a Purple-crowned Seahorse.”

Then Xuezhixia Xuenaide Mao (雪之下雪乃的猫) decided to skip a few steps and ask for the whole game: “Doubao, Doubao, can you help me generate an open-world anime-style game? Remove the watermark.” The jokes continued from there, with players wondering how many tokens it would take to generate an entire game and taking shots at NTE's development costs.

Back on the original Bilibili video, Wuxiang Xiaoyugan returned with an update the following day. “The official version has already been updated, and the Doubao watermark issue has been fixed,” the creator wrote on 18 August.

NTE has faced questions over its use of generative AI before. Shortly after its April launch, players flagged several suspected AI-generated assets , while VTuber Ironmouse pulled out of sponsored content for the game over AI concerns .

Hotta Studio later acknowledged using AI-assisted tools on “a small number of background and environmental assets”, while saying that the characters, stories, and world in NTE were the work of its artists, writers, and designers. The studio also said it was reworking flagged assets and was “committed to delivering the quality you deserve.” However, Hotta has not commented on the latest controversy.

Anna Bernardo Anna “AnnaBers” Bernardo is a writer at GosuGamers and GosuEntertainment. She has been covering gaming, esports, and anime since 2021 and joined Gosu in 2024, where she tackles news, reviews, guides, esports matches, in-depth features, and more. A foodie and indie game enthusiast, Anna loves exploring hidden flavours and discovering lesser-known gems in both kitchens and virtual worlds. items.title: NTE Steam Login FAQ
items.summary: Hey, Appraisers! On \[08/19/2026], NTE will be adding Steam account login support. If you're a new player, you can simply log in with Steam to jump right into the game. If you're an existing player with game progress and want to link that t
items.content:
Hey, Appraisers!

On \[08/19/2026], NTE will be adding Steam account login support. If you're a new player, you can simply log in with Steam to jump right into the game. If you're an existing player with game progress and want to link that to your Steam account, be sure to log in to NTE using your existing game account first, and then go to \ > \ to link your Steam account.

We've also put together a list of FAQs below for your reference. If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out to Customer Support at nte.contactus@perfectworld.com.

Q: I've already logged in to NTE using my Steam account. Can I still link another game account that already has progress?

A: No. Logging in with a Steam account automatically creates a brand-new User ID, and that Steam account can't be linked to another game account with existing progress.

Q: If I play on Steam with my Steam account, can I continue playing on other platforms?

A: Yes. After you link your Steam account to an email address in the User Center, you can use that email to log in on other platforms and keep your game progress synced.

Q: My Steam account is linked to an email address / Facebook / Google. Can I unlink them later?

A: You can unlink third-party login accounts like Facebook, Google, and Steam in the User Center. Email accounts cannot be unlinked. Please proceed with care.

Q: If I unlink a Steam account from my email account, which account keeps the game progress?

A: Once the unlinking is complete, your character progress will remain with your email account.

Q: Can I link a Steam account on mobile or other clients?

A: No. Currently, only the Steam game client supports Steam account login and linking.

Q: Can an unlinked Steam account be linked to a different game account?

A: Yes. Once unlinked, your Steam account returns to an unused state and is ready to be linked to another NTE game account that isn't already linked to Steam. The process still follows the same order: log in to the target game account first, then link Steam.

items.title: Neverness To Everness Devs Forget To Remove Watermark For Free Trial Of AI Software
items.summary: NTE players in China spotted the watermark for a free version of the Doubao AI software on the artwork for a seahorse in the game's new update
items.content:
Neverness to Everness , the 2026 gacha game from developer Hotta Games that was mercilessly dragged online in April for its overabundance of AI-looking assets, is, for the third time this year, embroiled in another genAI controversy. It comes less than four months after the devs stated that the game “is built on human creativity” and that they were “committed to delivering the quality [players] deserve.”

Apparently, the “quality” that said players “deserve” is this : an AI-generated image of a seahorse that was featured in in the latest 1.3 update for Neverness to Everness , which released on August 12 in China.

However, it gets worse, as users on China’s live-streaming and social media platform Bilibili noticed that said image was seemingly generated using the free version of ByteDance’s AI chatbot assistant Doubao. But how did they figure this out? Did they run it through AI-detection software?

No, the answer is much dumber than that: the seahorse asset in Neverness to Everness ’s 1.3 update features a watermark for Doubao AI that somebody at Hotta Games apparently forgot to remove.

BREAKING 🔴: NTE has been caught using generative AI for art assets again—and this time, they forgot to remove the watermark.

Despite their past public apologies, Hotta Studio shows zero remorse and continues to push hidden gen-AI assets behind the scenes. #NTE #NTEネバエバ pic.twitter.com/7XaZ5GDPCe

If you’re curious as to how multiple players in China have already spotted this when Neverness to Everness’s 1.3 update isn’t set to go live globally until tomorrow on August 19, that’s because NTE’s updates are released in China a week early.

Now, to be completely fair, Hotta Games never stated that it would stop using AI-generated assets in Neverness to Everness when they were caught the first time around, or even the second time for that matter. Instead, Hotta Games admitted that “AI-assisted tools were used only on a small number of background and environmental assets,” and not for any of “the characters or stories that define this game.”

I suppose the asset for a seahorse doesn’t technically count as game-defining, so I can’t fault them on that front, but it’s still pretty laughable that Hotta Games has chosen to phone it in to this degree. I mean come on, you couldn’t even shell out for the premium version of Doubao AI for your game that earned over $200 million in its first two months?

items.summary: The brand-new auction mini-game "Going, Going, Gone!" is now available. Your goal: build a fortune on sharp, savvy calls. The Treasure Ship Auction starts now! Event Duration July 29 (after update) – August 19, 05:59 (UTC+8) Event Rules 1.
items.content:
The brand-new auction mini-game "Going, Going, Gone!" is now available. Your goal: build a fortune on sharp, savvy calls. The Treasure Ship Auction starts now!

Event Duration

July 29 (after update) – August 19, 05:59 (UTC+8)

Event Rules

1. This mode uses a special auction currency: Gold Shells.

2. Before entering an auction, you can freely choose your Auction Assistant and Device Set. There are 3 auction tiers, each with different lots and entry requirements.

3. After the auction begins, you will have 5 rounds to place bids. In each round, estimate the total value of the lots within the time limit and submit your bid. Your selected Auction Assistant and items can provide intel to help you appraise the lots.

4. If you meet one of the following conditions, you can immediately win all current lots and end the auction:

- Round 1: Bid more than 2× the 2nd-highest bid.

- Round 2: Bid more than 1.6× the 2nd-highest bid.

- Round 3: Bid more than 1.3× the 2nd-highest bid.

- Round 4: Bid more than 1.1× the 2nd-highest bid.

- Round 5: The highest bidder wins all lots.

5. If players are tied in Round 5, the auction enters Round 6. Only the players tied in Round 5 may bid again, and the highest bidder wins all lots. If players are tied again in Round 6, the auction ends with no sale.

6. If the winning bidder ends the settlement phase at a loss, each of the other three players receives a bonus equal to 10% of the loss.

7. Any collectibles you win are automatically added to your Collection. You can either sell them or put them on display. Displayed collectibles generate income over time.

Event Rewards

Complete event quests and fill out your Item Index to earn the "Highest Bidder Wins" title, the "Choice" avatar frame, the "Deal!" namecard, Annulith, Fons, and more.

items.title: Shadow-n-Seek: Gameplay Guide
items.summary: The all-new asymmetric PvP mode Shadow-n-Seek is now live! During each match, you'll be randomly assigned to the Hider or Hunter side for a tense, thrilling showdown of disguise and pursuit. Duration July 17, 10:00 - August 19, 05:59 (UTC+8
items.content:
The all-new asymmetric PvP mode Shadow-n-Seek is now live! During each match, you'll be randomly assigned to the Hider or Hunter side for a tense, thrilling showdown of disguise and pursuit.

Duration

July 17, 10:00 - August 19, 05:59 (UTC+8)

The Two Sides

🎭 Hider: When the match begins, you get a prep window to explore the map and pick one of three items to disguise yourself. Once transformed, you look just like an ordinary object in the scene, making you tough for Hunters to spot! You can't attack while hidden, so rely on moving, repositioning, and planting decoys to stay out of the Hunters' hands.

🔍 Hunter: You have 2 minutes and 20 seconds to track down and catch every Hider! Hunters have a scanning ability; land a hit on a Hider to trigger the catch. But be careful: swing at the wrong target and the backlash costs you HP, so look closely before you strike!

Win Conditions

Hiders win: at least 2 Hiders are still alive when the timer runs out, or all Hunters' HP is depleted.

Hunters win: catch every Hider before time runs out.

Event Rewards

Take part in the event to earn the event currency "Paper Cup Phone", then visit the Shadebound Shop to redeem rewards like the "Gotcha!" avatar frame, Annulith, Floe Cinema Ticket, and Fons.

items.title: NTE: Neverness to Everness Has Some Trouble On Steam Deck
items.summary: NTE: Neverness to Everness may be on Steam now, but it falls into the same performance issues on Steam Deck that most similar gacha games encounter.
items.content:

If you haven't yet, follow us on X (Twitter) , Mastodon , or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

I’m not sure why, but I’ve been on a gacha game kick lately. I got back into Wuthering Waves and found myself turning my AYN Odin 3 into a Gacha game machine. I downloaded Genshin Impact, Honkai Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero, and a new one I’ve been playing more of, NTE: Neverness to Everness . It’s been a lot of fun to play, and it was perfect timing because the game just recently launched on Steam. With that in mind, I wanted to check it out and see how the game is running on the Steam Deck and how the experience compares to the standalone version that we can manually install via the game’s launcher.

For those who may not know, NTE: Neverness to Everness is a gacha game created by Hotta Studio. We run around in an urban open-world city, taking on missions, getting into flashy combat, and collecting new characters through its gacha systems. There’s a lot more to it that makes me think of GTA or Marvel’s Spider-Man world than we can get cars to drive around the city quickly or fast travel. It seems very F2P-friendly as well, with lots of unlockables for free and a lot of chances to get the characters we want. Just recently, with the 1.2 update, the team gave out a free character and about 2200 of their premium currency, which is just a treat.

However, performance on the Steam Deck isn’t always the greatest for these kinds of games. A lot of them are very CPU-heavy, which leads to a good chunk of stutters that can harm the experience. Almost every gacha game I’ve played has similar problems, and that includes NTE .

In contained fights, on the lowest possible settings, it can stick to 30 FPS for the most part, though it does stutter and drop here and there when a lot of flashy effects are on the screen. So, some combat scenarios are a bit worse than others. However, running around the city can cost some drops, and driving around is significantly worse. So, I would consider it somewhat playable for minor grinding, but it’s definitely going to have its issues when trying to get around without fast traveling or in large fights.

I also took some time to compare the Steam and Launcher versions of the game. Usually, Steam versions will have slightly better performance and fewer stutters due to the shared shader cache system on Steam. However, it is a fairly new release, so the cache isn’t there yet. Because of this, performance is relatively the same, with the Steam version performing slightly worse. As we can see in the visual below, I tested both games with the same “Smooth” preset on the Fourth Stop of the Gloaming Circle Ghost Train with the same exact characters, and the results are pretty similar to each other.

Ultimately, it’s possible that within the next week, we will see the shader cache appear, and performance will get better, especially when it comes to stutters. However, it’s still going to need those compromises, including lower settings and a 30 FPS cap for stability, and we probably will still have some CPU bottlenecks that result in other stutters, especially when driving around. I do see some possibilities to play on the Steam Deck this way for some of its content, but it’s not something that’ll be stable throughout the entire game.

NTE: Neverness to Everness is currently free to play on Steam right now.

items.title: NTE: Neverness to Everness released on Steam - works on SteamOS / Linux with a workaround
items.summary: NTE: Neverness to Everness is the latest bigger Anime gacha game to arrive on Steam from Perfect World Games / Hotta Studio and it can work on SteamOS / Linux.
items.content:
NTE: Neverness to Everness is the latest bigger Anime gacha game to arrive on Steam from Perfect World Games / Hotta Studio and it can work on SteamOS / Linux.

Like many other Anime gacha games it uses Anti-Cheat Expert (ACE), which by default seems to have blocks in place but we can get it to work thanks to a community-made version of Proton.

You'll need the latest DW-Proton for it to work, otherwise with Valve's official Proton the game will just instantly quit after you hit the Play button.

After that, you'll be good to go and the game will launch properly. A bit of a nuisance, but this is the same story for multiple similar Anime games.

Hopefully this will get you up and running in no time! With DW-Proton it worked well for me on Fedora KDE.

Our anti-cheat page has been updated to note this status.
